{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABamw_XA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhENVqU", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 97, "title": "Support i386/i486 MOV from control registers (0F 20) and diagnose Ap DOS HDD boot failure", "body": "## Problem

A user mounting a locally held PC-98 HDD image named `aliceY3.hdi` with the **PC-9821Ap DOS** profile reported:

```text
unimplemented i486 opcode 0F 20
```

This is a **runtime CPU emulation failure after the HDD image has been accepted**, not the earlier `Floppy image exceeds 4 MiB` error. Opcode `0F 20 /r` encodes `MOV r32, CRn`, reading an i386/i486 control register into a general-purpose register. However, the error string alone does **not** establish the ModR/M byte, control register number, guest CS:IP, preceding instruction stream, validity of the instruction, or whether mis-decoding/bad guest media was involved. Diagnose that before claiming any specific program behavior.

The current [`src/cpu.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/src/cpu.rs) implements `SMSW` (`0F 01 /4`) using a **16-bit `machine_status` field**, but `Cpu::extended` falls through to `unimplemented i486 opcode 0F 20` for control-register reads. The current Ap profile intentionally lacks protected mode, paging, DPMI and most CRn functionality; see [DOS compatibility scope](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/dos-compatibility.md).

This Issue addresses a real missing **386/486 CPU instruction and consistent status readback**, not a request to make all HDD images or Windows applications run.

## Expected outcome

Implement architecturally defensible **real-mode i386/i486 `MOV r32, CRn`** support in the existing original Rust CPU, including accurate decoding, supported CRn state and error behavior. Reconcile `CR0` readback with `SMSW`, existing x87 status checks, reset and machine profile. A small independent, redistributable DOS/native guest fixture must execute the instruction on the **Ap** profile in both native Rust and real production Wasm.

Separately, make the original user-reported HDD failure diagnosable: preserve precise CS:IP, opcode and following ModR/M/decoded register information in bounded local tracing. On a lawfully held local `aliceY3.hdi`, an implementer may verify whether this was a valid control-register read and whether execution progresses afterward, but **that HDD image is not required in CI or for merging**. If the program subsequently needs `MOV CRn,r32` (`0F 22`), protected mode, paging, extended DOS or additional machine behavior, **record the new evidence and file a separate `task` Issue**; do not silently fake those facilities or expand this Issue into comprehensive protected-mode support.

### Scope and correctness considerations

- Decode `0F 20 /r` under the **Ap** profile only, requiring register encoding (`ModR/M.mod = 3`) and correct 32-bit destination register handling regardless of the current real-mode default operand size, subject to verified i486 prefix legality. Correctly handle and test all accepted general registers, including ESP, and leave unrelated GPRs, segment state, flags, RAM and I/O unchanged.
- Determine supported control-register identifiers and reset values from architectural documentation. At minimum, implement the **architecturally valid CR0 read** that reveals the current real-mode status; do not incorrectly treat the 16-bit SMSW value as an entire 32-bit CR0. If CR2/CR3 reads are supported, represent their values coherently; do not invent support for undefined/unavailable control registers or unrelated CR4 behavior. Reject invalid encodings with the architecturally appropriate guest exception instead of silently returning fabricated data. Preserve the VM's V30 `0F` interpretation.
- Preserve the current intentional lack of protected execution and paging. Do not set control bits to imply a running protected-mode or paged environment, and do not add a filename-specific workaround.
- Verify correct instruction length, next IP, error-frame/restart address, instruction prefixes, register preservation and boundary cases. Use independent CPU specification references (e.g. Intel 80386/486 manuals), **not an existing emulator implementation**.
- Keep the original no-emulation-libraries policy; the CPU and devices remain implemented from scratch in Rust.

## Context and reproduction

Reported workflow:

1. Select `PC-9821Ap DOS` in the web emulator.
2. Select `IDE · HDI boot` and mount a locally held `aliceY3.hdi` image (not a floppy). The file's rights, origin, size, header and exact guest content have **not** been independently verified by this report.
3. After the initial `Floppy image exceeds 4 MiB` error was resolved by selecting IDE, the emulator reported `unimplemented i486 opcode 0F 20`.

The next diagnostic capture should record the exact tested commit, image format/geometry and a locally computed hash, machine profile, guest CS:IP, machine instruction bytes **as brief diagnostic opcode/ModR/M information only**, prefix/operand/address state, CRn selection and relevant CPU registers. Avoid publishing copyrighted game-code disassembly or complete memory dumps. Be mindful that invalid media or a wrong control-flow path could also reach `0F 20`.

Keep all third-party HDD/media, guest software, game assets, saves and detailed raw traces **outside Git and hosted CI/PR/Issues/Pages artifacts**. No proprietary BIOS, NEC ROM/font, copyrighted commercial game or manually provided disk image may be required for automated acceptance. Use an original MIT test guest and the repository's existing legal FreeDOS fixtures where appropriate.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reproduce the pre-fix `0F 20` unsupported behavior with an **independently authored, license-cleared minimal CPU probe**, not with `aliceY3.hdi`. The probe demonstrates that the same opcode is actually fetched and decoded as intended.
- [ ] Add original Rust instruction implementation for valid Ap real-mode `MOV r32, CRn` cases (at minimum CR0) using verified 386/486 semantics and reset state. Existing `SMSW`, x87 CR0 status checks, interrupt behavior and VM/V30 decoder remain consistent; no protected-mode/paging claims or fabricated register semantics.
- [ ] Native tests exercise all supported register destinations, CR0 full-width behavior, prefixes, flags/GPR preservation, invalid ModR/M and control-register selectors, guest #UD/error behavior, instruction length/IP/restart behavior, and reset. Document exactly which CRn selectors/prefix cases are supported.
- [ ] Original MIT guest code executes `0F 20` and reports a verifiable PASS through real guest execution on the Ap profile, natively and in the **production Rust/Wasm build** (both `/` and `/pc98-rust/` browser paths) with cold boot and reset checks, without host-substituted CPU results. Store the fixture source/license/hash and reproducible preparation in the existing guest-test conventions; do not publish restricted media.
- [ ] Preserve all existing VM, Ap, DOS/game, disk, sound and browser regressions. Run the applicable documented fixture preparation, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, production Wasm build and real-Wasm Chromium tests **before merge**. Report exact commands and outcomes.
- [ ] Document the present CRn, protected-mode and paging boundaries and the diagnostic methodology for the original HDD symptom. **If** a lawful local copy of the original image is accessible to the implementer, retest it privately and summarize the actual result, including any next missing opcode/mode; **otherwise** explicitly mark this optional local retest as not performed. Do not assert that this Issue fixes complete game boot or playability.
- [ ] No copied/ported emulator CPU/chip implementation, unlicensed media, game assets or proprietary ROMs enter the repository or published web tree; automated review verifies no unnecessary broad hardware scope.

All pre-merge acceptance must be verifiable automatically, without private HDD images, human testing, physical hardware, a live Pages URL or post-merge deployment. Follow the [repository development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md).

## Optional validation

Locally re-run the specific user-held `aliceY3.hdi` if legitimately available, compare to independent i486 documentation, and record subsequent boot blockers or protected-mode transitions as separate tasks. Do not distribute that media or make it a merge gate.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Any later deployed-site issue belongs in a separate `task` Issue and must not block this merge.
